board.title: Newsletter · the page · option 1 · Steps down the page
board.name: Steps down the page

drawn.title: Newsletter · the page · option 1 · Steps down the page
drawn.note: Option 1 puts the three steps (Write it, Check it, Send it) in white cards down the page, joined by a numbered line, and keeps the December email at the side in a small phone frame. It is best for a first-time sender, who always knows which step comes next and can see what members will get without leaving the page.
unresolved: The side column is about 50px shorter than the steps column, so a little cream space sits under the two quiet links. I left it because the preview frame stays put while the steps scroll.

To keep the board under 2300 tall, the computer page ends after More options with no site footer, and the message box is drawn scrolled to the Coming up lines (with a scrollbar) instead of showing the whole letter. The side preview shows the top of the email.

Step 2 is drawn without the 'Test sent at 2:09 PM' line from Newsletter-E, so each step has exactly one thing to do. Only step 1 carries a 'Step 1 of 3 · You are here' label. On steps 2 and 3, the numbered circles on the rail show the order.

Phone 1 shows the page with "See the email" docked at the foot. Phone 2 shows the preview brought up over the page, with "Back to writing". Every date, with its weekday: Sat, Dec 5, 2026; Sat to Mon, Jan 16 to 18, 2027; Sat, May 8, 2027; Sat to Mon, Sep 5 to 7, 2026 (in the box's hidden overflow and the sheet's lower part). Fixed by binding each separator dot to the word before it with a no-break space, keeping each pasted link's words together, and setting text-wrap:wrap on .p1-tin p, because the kit's text-wrap:pretty was pushing words down. Each link now sits whole on its own line after its event line.

Phones: added a grey caption under each phone, as the spec asks for captions under each frame: 'Writing · See the email waits at the foot of the screen.' and 'After pressing See the email · Back to writing closes it.'. I removed the LEFT and RIGHT label paragraphs from the side column and shortened its line to 'The same three steps, one under the other. One button, See the email, brings the email up over the page.'

Phone 2 sheet subline: changed 'The December email as it will arrive. It changes as you type.', which left 'you type.' alone on the second line, to 'The December email. It changes as you type.' on one line.
Phone 2 sheet: moved it up from 104px to 98px so the half-clipped 'Newsletter' heading no longer peeks above it. Only the dimmed crumb shows now.

The phone status bar in the side preview shows '2:15' without PM, as a real phone status bar does (the same convention as E-2's '8:04'). The page itself says 'Saved automatically at 2:15 PM'.
The phone page marks the progress with small '1 Write it / 2 Check it / 3 Send it' pills. They are page controls, not board chips, but a strict reading of 'no chips' could flag them.
I did not check the header pixel for pixel against Nav-Header-Final. The phone app bar matches Home-Final-Phones.

The three steps and the two send buttons sit in one slim bar across the top, so this option is best for someone who wants to watch each line turn into the finished email as they type it.

remaining_concerns: Options 1 and 3 are the closest pair at thumbnail size: both have a white card on the left and a phone-shaped preview on the right. They read apart at full size (stacked cards on a numbered rail versus a top stepper with one card and the two small step pictures), so I did not change either, but if K cuts to three, these two compete most directly.

The step words differ on purpose because the specs set them: 'Write it / Check it / Send it' in 1, 3 and 4, but 'Write / Check / Send' in 2 and 5. I left them as specified. If K wants the set fully uniform, the fix is two word changes in 2 and 5.

The desktop header now follows the decided rule for a 1200 frame (rook mark only, Search as icon plus word). That means the 'Louisiana Chess Association' name appears only in the phone headers and the email band. If K would rather the president see the name in the desktop bar too, that would break the decided header's width rule.
Option 5's side preview is the smallest of the five, about 180px of email visible inside the tabbed panel. It fits the compact spec, but it is the weakest answer to K's 'easy to see' ask.
Option 5's small preview has a thin scroll indicator drawn over the right end of the navy band. I left it because it is part of the original drawing, but it can read as a stray line at full size.
Option 4 has no 'More options' item list (only the closed button) because the bottom bar has no room. That matches its spec but reads a little differently from the other four.

The status line differs by design: 1 and 4 read 'December 2026 · Draft · Saved automatically at 2:15 PM', while 2, 3 and 5 read 'December 2026 · Draft' and show the saved note where their specs put it (bar, card foot, strip).
